subject: Clarifying plan portability, step-down credit and feature bundling options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kate Morales <kate@clearpoint.ai>, Procurement <procurement@clearpoint.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarifying plan portability, step-down credit and feature bundling options

Hi Kate / team —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. A few follow-ups from our side so we can put together a concise SOW and pricing sheet:

1) Portability: you asked about moving seats/features between tiers mid-contract — can you confirm whether you need the ability to move capacity across teams (same account) or between distinct legal entities? That changes how we surface entitlements in the portal.

2) Downgrade / step-down credits: is the ask that ClearPoint receives a token/credit pool if you reduce committed throughput mid-term, or are you after a one-time rollback credit against next invoice?

3) Feature bundling: which premium features matter most (rate-limited dedicated routes, extended audit retention, private VPC control-plane)? If you rank top 2 I can map them to a single add-on SKU.

To speed things up Im attaching a draft pricing-model (spreadsheet) and a placeholder SOW. If you can share expected monthly TPS and peak tokens/day, well produce three options: Minimal commit (metered + small burst), 12-month commit (discounted), and Bridge Pack (12-month hybrid with downgrade protection).

Proposed next step: 30-minute pricing alignment early next week. Are you available Tue/Wed morning PT?

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachments: ClearPoint_SOW_v2.docx (draft), pricing-model.xlsx (usage template)

From: Kate Morales <kate@clearpoint.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying plan portability, step-down credit and feature bundling options

Ben —

Thanks for the follow-up. Quick answers inline: 

- Portability: between teams within the same legal entity only. We will not move entitlements to another company.
- Step-down credits: our procurement prefers a credit pool applied pro-rata to future invoices (not a cash refund). Important that we can see the credit balance in the billing portal.
- Feature bundling: priority is (1) extended audit retention to 365 days, and (2) private VPC control-plane for sensitive workflows.

Wed like to see concrete language in the SOW about downgrade behavior — specifically: within the first 6 months of a 12-month commit, if we reduce committed throughput, we receive credits equal to 40% of remaining committed value to apply to future invoices. Does Redwood have standard wording for that?

Also, heads-up from procurement: any discount >15% will likely need legal approval and an exec sign-off. Can you flag that?

I can do Tue 9:30am PT for a call.

—Kate
Kate Morales
Head of Product, ClearPoint Analytics
kate@clearpoint.ai

Requests: Please include the SOW and a SKU list in the follow-up.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Kate Morales <kate@clearpoint.ai>, Procurement <procurement@clearpoint.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarifying plan portability, step-down credit and feature bundling options — ClearPoint ask

Lauren / Priyom —

Looping you both in on ClearPoints asks so we can finalize the offer before Tuesday's call. Short summary: 

- They want portability across teams (same legal entity).
- They want downgrade credits applied to future invoices and visible in portal; procurement expects a 40%-of-remaining-commit credit for downgrades within first 6 months of a 12-month commit.
- Priority add-ons: 365-day audit retention, private control-plane.
- Procurement says discounts >15% need legal/exec approval.

My suggestion for the call: present three priced options (short bullets below) and confirm which ones require exception approvals so I can escalate: 

A) Metered + Burst: no commit; standard add-on pricing. No step-down credits.
B) Standard 12-mo Commit: 15% list discount, add-ons a la carte, downgrade handled by prorated billing only (no credits).
C) Bridge Pack (customer requested): 12-mo commit with 12% higher base commit for first 3 months (to cover onboarding peaks), 15% discount, and a step-down credit equal to 40% of unused committed spend if downgraded within 0-6 months. Includes one bundled premium add-on (audit=365d).

Questions for you: can we approve C with up to 15% discount and the 40% step-down credit as a Sales Ops-approved concession, or do we need exec sign-off? If no, what's the minimum approval path (who signs)? Also, if we include the private control-plane, is that technically feasible to deliver as a single add-on SKU or do we need a scoping engagement?

Forwarding Kate's note below for context.

On Thu, Sep 30, 2026 at 11:05 AM Kate Morales <kate@clearpoint.ai> wrote:
> Ben —
> 
> Thanks for the follow-up. Quick answers inline: ...

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: Kate Morales <kate@clearpoint.ai>, Procurement <procurement@clearpoint.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarifying plan portability, step-down credit and feature bundling options — ClearPoint ask

Ben / Lauren —

Thanks for the context. Proposed commercial position and next steps below — Ive attached an updated SOW and a clean pricing-model for the call.

Recommended offer (we can present as a single-line "Bridge Pack" or break it into two SKUs):

- Term: 12 months commit.
- Discount: 15% off list (Sales-approved). Any additional discount requires VP approval (route: Priyom -> Lauren -> VP Sales).
- Step-down credit: If customer reduces committed throughput within first 6 months, Redwood will grant a credit equal to 40% of the unused committed spend (applies only to invoice credits, visible in billing portal). After month 6, downgrade is prorated with no additional credit.
- Bundling: include one premium add-on (365d audit retention) in the Bridge Pack at a bundled price (explicit SKU). Private control-plane remains an optional add-on requiring scoping; well mark it as "requires technical review" in the SOW.
- Portability: allow entitlement transfers between teams within the same legal entity. Transfers between legal entities are disallowed without a contract amendment.

Operational notes:
- We'll implement a billing-portal flag to surface credit balance; Engineering needs a small billing-API task (estimate: 2 sprints).
- SOW: scope private control-plane as an optional milestone with separate acceptance criteria.

Attachments: ClearPoint_SOW_v2.docx (SOW with downgrade language), pricing-model.xlsx (three-option workbook).

Next steps: Ben, lead Tue 9:30am PT call — present the Bridge Pack and confirm the customer's desired add-on (audit vs private control-plane). If the customer requests both included at sign, I will escalate for VP approval for any extra discount.

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
